slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Measure a hill's steepness with a clinometer.

Goal: I can define and use tangent.

geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Measure a hill's steepness with a clinometer.

Goal: I can define and use tangent.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
For an acute angle A of a right triangle, tan A = (leg opposite A)/(leg adjacent to A).

Use it to find a leg: if a hill rises at 12 degrees for a horizontal run of 200 m, the rise is 200 tan 12 degrees, about 200 times 0.2126 = 42.5 m.

A clinometer measures the angle; a tape measures the run. Note that tan A is the slope of the hypotenuse when the adjacent leg is horizontal.
